<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par138" />''founded'' (it) ''for them''; on the same analogy we may also take, with Baumann (op. cit., p. 48), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=54}}, ({{GHGheb|text=חַר זֶה}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַם־זוּ גָאָ֑לְתָּ}}), 15:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=142|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=143|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (all examples of {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|h}}
To introduce independent relative clauses {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} is used as a nominative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=19}}; as accusative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=17}} and {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=29}} (after a preposition, {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=8}}; but the text is evidently corrupt).

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|i}}
(''b'') More certain examples of the use of the article as a relative pronoun (more correctly, perhaps, of the demonstrative which is otherwise used as article) are {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=26|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל הַֽהִקְדִּישׁ שְׁמוּאֵל|translate=all that Samuel had dedicated}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=8}} (where {{GHGheb|text=נִמְצָא}} can only be {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=14}}. In connexion with a plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=24}} ''the chiefs of the men of war'' {{GHGheb|text=הֶהָֽלְכוּ אִתּוֹ|translate=who went with him}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=17}}. Finally, in the sense of ''id quod'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=13}} (where, however, we should read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=הַדָּבָר}}). Cf. moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=24}} ''the thigh'' {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽעָלֶ֫יהָ|translate=and that which was upon it}} (but see k below); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֵכִין}} equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר הֵכִין|translate=to the place, that he had prepared}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|k}}
In all the examples adduced except {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=24}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וְהָֽאַלְיָה}} should probably be read for {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽעָלֶ֫יהְ}} the {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} is followed by undoubted perfects; almost all the examples, moreover, belong to the latest Books (Ezra and Chronicles). On the other hand, another series of instances (even in the older texts) is extremely doubtful, in which the Masora likewise requires perfects, either by placing the tone on the penultima, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=27|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּ֫אָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׂ֫מָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֻלָּ֫לָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=6|hidebook=1}} and 4:3 {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׁ֫בָה}}, or by the punctuation, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנּוֹלַד}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּרְאָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּלְוָה}}, while no doubt the authors in all these cases intended participles (and in fact perfect participles, cf. {{GHGpar|116|d}}) with the article, thus {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּאָ֫ה}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֻלָּלָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַמְהֻלָּלָה}} according to {{GHGpar|52|s}}, and in the other examples {{GHGheb|text=הַנּוֹלָד}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּרְאֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּלְוֶה}}.
<section end="par138" />
<section begin="par139" />{{GHGpar-heading|139|Expression of Pronominal Ideas by means of Substantives}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|a}}
Analogous to the periphrases for expressing materials and attributes by means of substantives ({{GHGpar|128|o}} and p), is the use of substantives to represent certain kinds of pronominal ideas, for which no special expressions exist. Thus—

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|b}}
'''1.''' {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=man, woman}}, are used to express—

(''a'') The idea of ''each, every'' (in the sense of each severally) with reference to persons,<ref>As a rule {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} is used in the particularizing sense of ''each man'', with the plural of the verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=11}}; sometimes, however, as subject to a verb in the singular, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=13}}.</ref> and even animals ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=10}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=10|verse=5}}, feminine {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} is the object, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=15}}. On {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}—{{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} cf. {{GHGpar|123|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|c}}
In a few passages {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} in the above sense is placed for the sake of emphasis before the governing noun (always a substantive with a suffix), thus {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד אִישׁ אָחִיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=5}}, according to the usual explanation, stands for {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד אֲחִי אִישׁ|translate=at the hand of the brother of every man}}. But although the explanation seems to be<section end="par139" /><noinclude>
